findings.title: raw_html cook method stores unsanitized HTML as cooked post
findings.body: Post#cook now returns the raw text verbatim when cook_method is :raw_html, which means the cooked column contains completely unsanitized HTML imported from RSS feeds (PollFeed) and remote pages (TopicRetriever -> TopicEmbed.import_remote). That cooked HTML is then rendered unescaped in app/views/embed/best.html.erb via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (and anywhere else cooked posts are shown), so any feed entry or embedded page can inject arbitrary JavaScript — a stored XSS that executes in the browsers of visitors on the embedding site (via the iframe) and of forum users viewing the imported topic. The content is never passed through Sanitize/PrettyText, so there is no script stripping at any point.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring match and can be bypassed
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` does a substring check instead of an exact origin comparison. An origin like `https://forum.example.com.evil.com` (or any host whose origin string appears inside discourseUrl) passes the check, allowing a malicious page to send crafted `discourse-resize` messages. It should compare `e.origin` exactly against the parsed origin of discourseUrl.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is the full referer URL, so resize messages are never delivered
findings.body: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the entire referer URL (including path, e.g. `http://blog.example.com/2013/02/10/post.html`) as targetOrigin. Browsers only accept an origin (scheme + host + port) or '*' as targetOrigin; a URL with a path will not match the parent's origin, so the message is silently dropped and the iframe is never resized (the resize mechanism this whole feature depends on does not work). Use only the origin portion of the referer.

findings.title: Editing an old migration to add force: true drops the existing top_topics table
findings.body: The already-applied migration CreateTopTopics was changed from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. On any environment where this migration re-runs (e.g. rebuilt databases, or deployments where migration state is reset), force: true will DROP and recreate the existing top_topics table, destroying all stored top-topic statistics. Old migrations should never be edited; unrelated 'force: true' additions to MigrateWordCounts/new migrations are fine, but this one alters a shipped migration.

findings.title: Feed items without content element crash the hourly job
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a `content` element. Many RSS feeds only provide `description`, in which case SimpleRSS returns nil for content and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError. Since the job runs hourly with retry disabled, one such feed item kills the entire polling run and no topics get imported until the offending item scrolls out of the feed.

findings.title: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever but the controller enqueues a background job
findings.body: The spec 'tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found' sets `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, but EmbedController#best never instantiates TopicRetriever — it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, and in the test environment jobs are not executed. This expectation can never be satisfied by the real code path, so the test either fails or was written against an older synchronous implementation; it should instead assert that the :retrieve_topic job is enqueued with the right arguments.

findings.title: import mutates the caller's contents string with <<
findings.body: `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."` appends the 'imported from' footer directly to the string passed in by the caller. Any caller that reuses that string (e.g. a loop variable or a comparison against the original feed content) will see it unexpectedly modified. Duplicate the string before appending (e.g. `contents = contents.dup` or `contents +=`).
